statement: Assume ℓ < ∞, and use the guarded diagonal constructed above. One can retain all but o(1) of the relative mass of the original final path and choose an interior parent window with the following properties. Write d = d∗, N = Nϵn 0 , and use K = No(1) for analytical estimates. There is one prepared path probability µprep = P A pAλ0 A, where pA = µprep{A} and λ0 A is its conditional probability in parent A. On the retained parents, λ0 A ≤ KνA × dt, where νA is the prior conditioned on the full parent trajectory assignment and dt is uniform parent time. Subsequent omissions restrict this mixture and leave its reference weights and probabilities fixed. 53 1. At every required bounded tangent depth s, the true label Qs has thickness as = N−s, time length qs ∼log,N N−ks, and spatial determinant Js ∼log,N qj sN−ℓs in version 2; omit the last factor in version 1. Its largest width is comparable to qs in logarithmic order, and its full assigned trajectory mass satisfies νQ ∼log,N ad sJs. 2. For the restricted incidence laws, pure hidden and native-signal bins of width p have the instantaneous joint base-density ceiling Kpd on the required finite grids. In unit coordinates of a Qs-box, the base marginal has density at most KqsνQ, with masses still measured in parent time. 3. Let v = V in version 1 and in the case ℓ = 0. For 0 < ℓ < ∞, let Z, Y be the major and minor parent coordinates and put v = Z′. The fixed conditional parent palette πA, the velocity marginal of λ0 A, satisfies πA(Bp) ≤ KpS. If E denotes the end history, then before likelihood deletion the required velocity bin satisfies X A pAIλ0 A ([v]; E) = o(log N). Thus the information bound is averaged with the fixed parent weights. 4. Required finite-mesh point states and path labels have lists at the original pL bounded by fixed powers of actual path factors and logarithms. Sufficiently deep histories leave only K options for these point states. Each fitted test has at most K local graph choices approximating w to Kas on retained incidences in their cores. After composition with the native test, their fixed-order derivatives are bounded by K on the used normalized interiors. These graph bounds and capped full-layer incidence witnesses can be prepared before arbitrary later inverse-subpower selections. When 0 < ℓ < ∞, major-coordinate fullness and the coefficients of the tilted-box rows can be prepared with actual N0-subpower bounds. The joint and conditional consequences of these fixed laws are stated in Lemma 4.8 below.
